title: Gambling
note: Like drinking, gambling and illness come between a person and righteousness, wealth and pleasure. This chapter starts on those two with the nature of gambling.

couplets.plain: Don’t want gambling, even if you win. Your winnings are a hook swallowed by a fish.
couplets.pm: Even if you have the skill to win, don’t want gambling. Winning isn’t sure, and many tasks are ruined. If you say some do get winnings, those are like the iron hook, hidden in bait, that a fish swallows thinking it food. What you win is a shackle that keeps gamblers from leaving, and pain follows.

links.quote: Your winnings are a hook swallowed by a fish
Don’t want gambling, even if you win

couplets.plain: Gamblers gain one and lose a hundred. Can they have any way to gain good and live?
couplets.pm: Gamblers gain one thing, like that metal on the hook, and in the hope of more lose a hundred and end up poor. Can they have any way of living with the righteousness and pleasure that wealth gives? No. Their wealth keeps going, so they get none of what it brings.

links.quote: gain one and lose a hundred

couplets.plain: Keep on calling the throws of the rolling dice, and your wealth and income will leave and go to others.
couplets.pm: If a ruler keeps calling the throws of the rolling dice and gambles, the wealth he has gathered and the income it brings leave him and settle with his enemies. He gives no thought to keeping or to making, so both pass to them.

links.quote: your wealth and income will leave and go to others
links.reason: Constant betting moves your wealth and income into other hands.

couplets.plain: Nothing brings poverty like gambling, which shrinks you in many ways and ruins your good name.
couplets.pm: Gambling brings those who crave it many pains they didn’t have before, and ruins the fame they do have. Nothing else can give poverty like it. It takes away good deeds and good company, and brings bad deeds and bad company. Gamblers reach the limit of poverty.

links.reason: Ranks it the surest road to poverty, shrinking you and ruining your good name.

couplets.plain: Those who cling in their pride to dice, gaming hall and skill of hand have come to nothing.
couplets.pm: Rulers who took up the dice, the gaming floor and the skill of hand it needs, and wouldn’t let go, once were and then were no more. The skill is holding and throwing so as to land a winning score. He shows this from experience: through such clinging the Pandavas gave up their kingdom, went to the forest and lived there in hiding.

links.reason: Allows no exception: those who cling in pride to dice have come to nothing.

couplets.plain: Those covered over by the goddess of misfortune called gambling won’t fill their bellies, and will suffer.
couplets.pm: Her own name is unlucky to say, so she is called gambling. Those she swallows won’t fill their bellies in this life, and will suffer the pain of hell in the next. Like her, gambling takes wealth and gives poverty. Watching wins and losses they never leave the game, so they go hungry. They earn sins such as lying and theft, so they suffer.

links.quote: won’t fill their bellies, and will suffer
the goddess of misfortune called gambling
links.reason: Makes gambling a disguise of Fortune’s dark sister, who covers over those she takes.

couplets.plain: If your time goes into the gaming hall, it destroys the wealth and good nature you have long had.
couplets.pm: If a ruler’s time, meant for righteousness, wealth and pleasure, is spent on the gaming floor, it takes away the wealth that has come down to him and his good qualities. Not only what he would make himself goes, but also the wealth begun by his forebears and the good nature that is the fruit of past good deeds.

links.quote: destroys the wealth and good nature you have long had
links.reason: Time in the gaming hall eats up long-held wealth and good nature.

couplets.plain: Gambling destroys your wealth, makes you take up lying, destroys your compassion, and leaves you to suffer.
couplets.pm: Gambling destroys the wealth of the one who takes to it, makes him take up lying, destroys the compassion that rises in the mind, and so makes him suffer in both lives. Its tools are defeat, victory and hatred, in that order. The first brings suffering in this life, the others in the next.

links.quote: destroys your wealth, makes you take up lying
links.reason: Follows the damage in order: wealth, then truth, then compassion, then suffering.

couplets.plain: Clothes, wealth, food, glory and learning: these five won’t come near you if you take to dice.
couplets.pm: If a ruler takes up gambling as his pastime, glory, learning, wealth, food and clothing won’t come near him. Wealth means the six parts of the state. Food and clothing stand for all comforts. He has neither the time nor the mind for them, so they don’t come.

links.quote: won’t come near you if you take to dice

links.reason: Glory is on the list of what won’t come to the gambler.
Learning is on the list too, among the five that stay away.
Wealth is among the five that won’t come to the gambler.

couplets.plain: As gambling is loved more with each loss, so the soul loves more with each pain.
couplets.pm: As a gambler loves gambling more each time he loses the fruits of both lives, so the soul loves the body more each time it suffers the three kinds of pain through it. It seems to speak of the soul’s ignorance, but it means the gambler’s, and the comparison presses this home. The soul that turns from the body is like the man who turns from gambling.

links.quote: As gambling is loved more with each loss

ideaLinks.reason: Gambling destroys wealth, and nothing else brings poverty as it does.
Gambling makes you take up lying.
Gambling ruins your good name, and glory won’t come to those who take to it.
